newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, gasoline weaker.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, gasoline weaker.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Tuesday, with gasoline and gas oil weaker and naphtha firmer, traders said.
Naphtha continued to rise on fresh end-user demand in NWE and good refiner interest was also seen for cargoes into Lavera.
In addition to improving local demand, Petrobras was reported to be loading a large cargo at Skikda and is also expected to be seeking more product later in the month.
A second Egyptian Alex cargo traded into Lavera at high cif +$2.75 a tonne and a Tunis fob stem were heard offered around high cif $5-6.
Gasoline was easier. A couple of cargoes were available, out of Italy and France, but nothing was heard done.
Cargoes were notionally easier by $2 or so at $209-212 fob.
"European demand is fairly sparse so product really has to move to the U.S. and because freight is so expensive (close to $20 a tonne) I think Med numbers will have to ease," said a trader.

High sulphur cracked fuel oil was notionally stronger and cargoes pegged at around $114 fob Med. Bunker demand was still good in the region with little product seen available to cover it. One requirement was seen into Genoa for second half Jan.
Low sulphur fuel oil was steady, with good avails in northwest Europe and the U.S. keeping a lid on prices. Offers from NWE were seen at or slightly below $130 cif Italy.

Gas oil shed around $2.25 in line with futures in inactive trade. French and Italian heating oil demand was thin but ideas about premiums were steady at around high cif quotes +$2 basis Genoa, with traders seeing bids at +$1 and offers around +$2.50.
A European major bought a cargo of Italian grade heating oil at fob quotes +$3.50 basis Sicily.
